title: Hairdresser Confessions; Da Kink In My Hair Is Not Curled As Tight As It Once

display_heading.headline: Hairdresser Confessions
display_heading.deck: Da Kink In My Hair Is Not Curled As Tight As It Once Was

contact_edits.before: The most piercing speech of all, as it was in the original, is that of the young Trinidadian girl who was overjoyed to be brought to Canada to join her mother, and who then found herself being abused by her stepfather. I never expected to find a performance in this role that rivalled that of dbi.young, but Thais Francis is equally moving, both in her initial joy and in her later shame and terror. Unfortunately she's subjected, like everyone in the cast only more so, to amplification that makes her sound as if her voice were coming from some place else. Presumably the face mics are there for the musical sections, but it's shameful to keep them on for the dialogue; the Enwave is not exactly a big theatre. It adds to the feeling that the songs and dances aren't earning their keep. (There's already a musical about hair, and several about kinks.) Giving each character both a speech and a song makes the show feel repetitive; this, on top of the pacing problems already noted, makes it feel long. ? da Kink in My Hair runs through Aug. 21 at the Enwave Theatre, Harbourfront. Call 416-973-4000 or visit tickets.harbourfrontcentre.com for ticket information.
